current_row.boundary_rationale: The address shifts explicitly from the envoys of five nations to Judah’s own king, וְאֶל צִדְקִיָּ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי כְּכָל הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לֵאמֹ֑ר (oshb:Jer.27.12, byte), matching “I spoke to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these words, saying,” (web:Jer.27.12) — the same sign now applied directly to Zedekiah rather than relayed through foreign messengers. The rationale continues without a break through the question “Why will you die, you and your people, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, as Yahweh has spoken concerning the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?” (web:Jer.27.13), then through a negative-listening directive and its false-prophecy clause standing inside the span itself, וְאַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י הַנְּבִאִ֗ים הָאֹמְרִ֤ים אֲלֵיכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תַעַבְד֖וּ אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖ם נִבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.27.14, byte), matching “Don’t listen to the words of the prophets who speak to you, saying, ‘You shall not serve the king of Babylon;’ for they prophesy a lie to you.” (web:Jer.27.14). It closes on כִּ֣י לֹ֤א שְׁלַחְתִּים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה וְהֵ֛ם נִבְּאִ֥ים בִּשְׁמִ֖י לַשָּׁ֑קֶר לְמַ֨עַן הַדִּיחִ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ וַאֲבַדְתֶּ֔ם אַתֶּ֕ם וְהַנְּבִאִ֖ים הַֽנִּבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.27.15, byte), matching “For I have not sent them,” says Yahweh, “but they prophesy falsely in my name; that I may drive you out, and that you may perish, you, and the prophets who prophesy to you.” (web:Jer.27.15). A new address opens at verse 16, וְאֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים֩ וְאֶל כָּל הָעָ֨ם הַזֶּ֜ה דִּבַּ֣רְתִּי לֵאמֹ֗ר (oshb:Jer.27.16, byte) — from Zedekiah to the priests and the people generally, over a different object, the temple vessels — and this row does not reach past that turn.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this row into the surrounding relayed message as one continuous span was rejected because the address plainly narrows here to Zedekiah by name, in Jeremiah’s own first-person report, rather than continuing the third-person instruction to send word through envoys.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Hananiah performs a counter-act without any intervening narration, וַיִּקַּ֞ח חֲנַנְיָ֤ה הַנָּבִיא֙ אֶת הַמּוֹטָ֔ה מֵעַ֕ל צַוַּ֖אר יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֑יא וַֽיִּשְׁבְּרֵֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.28.10, byte), matching “Then Hananiah the prophet took the bar from off the prophet Jeremiah’s neck, and broke it.” (web:Jer.28.10). His own words follow at once, opening on the bare koh-amar shape rather than the tsevaot-plus-Elohei-Yisrael stack named two verses earlier: כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ כָּ֣כָה אֶשְׁבֹּ֞ר אֶת עֹ֣ל נְבֻֽכַדְנֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֗ל בְּעוֹד֙ שְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֔ים מֵעַ֕ל צַוַּ֖אר כָּל הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (oshb:Jer.28.11, byte), matching “Yahweh says: ‘Even so I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from off the neck of all the nations within two full years.’” (web:Jer.28.11) — the defective, vav-less spelling of Nebuchadnezzar’s name stands in these bytes, named here rather than left silent. A petuchah and a paseq both fall in this same verse (WLC, single-witness). A fresh word-event formula turns the scene to Yahweh’s own word to Jeremiah starting at verse 12, and this row ends just ahead of that turn.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Counting this verse’s formula toward the book’s roster of Yahweh’s own koh-amar onsets without disclosing its speaker was rejected on the same ground established at the formula standing at verse 2 and confirmed by the word event opening at verse 12: the mouth at verse 11 is Hananiah’s own, not Yahweh’s directly.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh word-event formula opens the unit, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֑ה אַ֠חֲרֵי שְׁב֞וֹר חֲנַנְיָ֤ה הַנָּבִיא֙ אֶת הַמּוֹטָ֔ה מֵעַ֗ל צַוַּ֛אר יִרְמְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.28.12, byte), matching “Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, after Hananiah the prophet had broken the bar from off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.28.12) — Yahweh’s own word to Jeremiah, occasioned by Hananiah’s own act just narrated. A commissioned reply follows, כִּ֣י כֹֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עֹ֣ל בַּרְזֶ֡ל נָתַ֜תִּי עַל צַוַּ֣אר כָּל הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֗לֶּה לַעֲבֹ֛ד אֶת נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל (oshb:Jer.28.14, byte), matching “For Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says,” “I have put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon” (web:Jer.28.14) — the same defective, vav-less spelling of Nebuchadnezzar’s name recurs in this reply as it did in the claim it answers. Verse 15 turns from Yahweh’s commissioned word to Jeremiah’s own delivery of it, marked by the same reply-formula that opened his first answer to Hananiah at verse 5, so the row is held to this commissioned content alone.
